newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky resigns.
newsitem.headline: Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky resigns.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky resigned on Saturday and said Finance Minister Viktor Klima had been designated as his successor.
Asked if he had resigned, Vranitzky said: "Of course. Klima on my proposal has been designated as federal chancellor."
"I have informed the party (leadership) of my intention to withdraw from all my political duties including the post of federal chancellor and they have accepted it," Vranitzky told reporters.
He said the party had also accepted his proposal that Klima should succeed him.
Vranitzky, Europe's second longest-serving leader after German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, made his announcement after a two-hour meeting of senior members of his Social Democrat Party.

Vranitzky, 59, took over the Austrian government in June 1986 and his Social Democrats have ruled in an uneasy coalition for most of that time with the conservative People's Party led by Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel.
